brief: The Market Ear argues the AI-led equity selloff is showing signs of exhaustion. NDX futures printed an unusual hammer candle and SOX is testing both the lower boundary of its trading range and its longer-term trend line after crashing, both read as sellers losing control. Goldman's Lin reports aggressive global de-risking, net flows at -2.1 standard deviations and long sales outpacing shorts roughly 3 to 1, with the US 66% of global selling and tech leading. Global AI stocks had their second-largest net selling day in a year (-2.8 Z-score). Hedge funds have net sold AI stocks for five straight sessions, erasing their entire 2025 net accumulation. AI allocation has fallen to 26.1% (49th percentile) and the long/short ratio to 3.27 (7th percentile), still a large position but much less crowded. KOSPI is at its most oversold level since October 2022. CoreWeave's November $95 call has collapsed from $18 to $1 since September 8, and the options unwind may have amplified the stock's drop as dealers sold to hedge. Separately, Russell 2000 hedge fund shorts have grown with widening CDX high-yield spreads since July, leaving short positioning crowded enough that a sharp covering rally is plausible.
